task.description:
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-checked rework iteration 1 (commit a4af506e). The rework1 fix to §3.1/§3.1a for Definitions' activate/2, deprecate/2, archive/2 is CORRECT and independently re-verified this session (see point 1 below) -- that part of the prior FAIL is genuinely closed. But this recheck found TWO further problems in rework 1's own new text, one of which is the SAME false-claim defect class as the original FAIL, now recurring in a different spot of the same rework. This is the second rework round on this exact defect class -- be precise and do not introduce a third occurrence.

1. VERIFIED CORRECT, do not touch: §3.1a's Decision (b) point 1 -- the AC11-infeasibility argument for widening activate_opts()/opts(). Re-read lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex directly this session: handle_activate/1 (line 923), handle_deprecate/1 (line 962), handle_archive/1 (line 972), and handle_delete/2's deprecate/archive branch (lines 857-883) all build their opts purely from conn.assigns.scoped_opts and never read conn.assigns.auth_context.user_id, whereas handle_import/1 (line 1003) and handle_rollback/2 (line 1121) do read it. Widening the three lifecycle functions' opts to carry a real actor_id would genuinely require editing these three router-file functions, which AC11 forbids. This reasoning is sound and needs no rework.

2. NEW FALSE/UNSUPPORTED CLAIM (same defect class as the original FAIL) -- §3.1a Decision (b)'s justification point 2 states as fact that 'Definitions.activate/2 is also called from system/scheduler-initiated paths with no HTTP request and no human actor at all,' citing test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs:135 and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs:100. Checked this session: `grep -rn "Definitions.activate(" lib/` (excluding the design doc itself) returns exactly ONE production call site -- lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex:926, inside handle_activate/1, i.e. the router/HTTP path. There is NO production scheduler-driven or system-driven caller of Definitions.activate/2 anywhere in lib/. The two cited test lines are test-fixture SETUP HELPERS (`active_definition!/1` in scheduler_test.exs, an equivalent helper in poller_test.exs) that call `Definitions.activate/2` directly from test code to build a fixture an unrelated scheduler/poller test then exercises -- they are not evidence of any real scheduler-initiated production code path invoking activate/2. Citing test setup code as proof of a production 'system/scheduler-initiated path with no human actor' materially overstates what the citation supports, the same failure mode (a citation asserted to support more than it actually shows) that produced the original FAIL on this design.

   Fix required: either (a) delete justification point 2 entirely -- point 1 (AC11 scope) is on its own a sufficient, fully-verified basis for Decision (b), so point 2 is not load-bearing and can simply be dropped -- or (b) rewrite point 2 to state accurately that no production caller of activate/2 (or deprecate/2, archive/2) other than the router currently exists, and that the two cited tests only demonstrate the functions CAN be invoked with no actor context available (test-harness evidence of shape, not evidence of an existing production system-driven path). Do not leave the current overstated wording in place.

3. SECOND REAL GAP -- the 'not verified this session' actor_id rows for the Identity module in the current §3.2 table (User create, User status/profile change, Group create, Token issue, Token revoke) are NOT actually unresolved. Checked this session directly against lib/letflow/identity.ex: `create_user/2` (line 218), `update_user_profile/3` (line 291), `update_user_status/3` (line 312), `create_group/2` (line 347), `create_token/3` (line 842), and `revoke_token/2` (line 929) ALL take `opts :: opts()` where `@type opts :: [prefix: String.t()]` (or equivalent narrow prefix-only opts) -- none of them has an actor_id parameter, keyword option, or field anywhere in their signature or body. This is the exact same gap as Definitions' three lifecycle functions, and it was trivially checkable (six function reads) -- it should not have been left as deferral language ('not verified this session', 'not this rework's job to redo') when the answer is now known and matches the already-established §3.1a pattern exactly. Per this project's design-completeness rule, a flagged uncertainty that ships to ELIXIR-DEV unresolved is still a gap, not a formality, especially once verification is this cheap and conclusive.

   Fix required: for all six of `Letflow.Identity.create_user/2`, `update_user_profile/3`, `update_user_status/3`, `create_group/2`, `create_token/3`, `revoke_token/2`'s audit rows in §3.2's table, replace 'not verified this session' with an explicit `actor_id: nil` disposition, stated the same way §3.1a states it for Definitions' three functions (schema-legal per §1.1, does not violate any acceptance criterion naming these operations -- note AC2 does not name any Identity operation, only activate/cancel/complete, so there is no AC2 conflict to reconcile here at all). Add a short subsection (e.g. §3.1b, or fold into §3.1a's own text renamed to cover both) stating this decision once, then have the table rows reference it, exactly as the Definitions rows now reference §3.1a -- do not repeat the full reasoning six times in the table cells. Track it under OQ-4 (or a new OQ-5) as the same class of deferred router/API-widening work as Definitions, if a future requirement wants to thread real actor attribution through these six functions too.

4. Leave the Task-create row's actor_id note as-is -- it is downstream of OQ-1 (exact call site not pinned, already accepted as a non-blocking open question on the ORIGINAL validator pass, unrelated to this rework), and this session's own check of lib/letflow/engine.ex did not find an unambiguous single insertion site either, so 'not independently verified this session' remains an honest statement there, unlike the six Identity functions above whose signatures are fully known and were simply not read.

5. Do not rewrite anything else. §1/§1.2/§1.3, §2, §4, §5, §6, §7, §8, the traceability matrix (§0), and OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-3 remain exactly as passed on the prior two validator passes -- re-confirmed byte-identical via diff this session, out of scope for this rework.
acceptance_criteria: §3.1a Decision (b)'s justification no longer asserts, as an established fact, that Definitions.activate/2 (or deprecate/2, archive/2) is called from a real production system/scheduler-initiated path -- either the claim is removed, or rewritten to accurately describe the two cited tests as fixture-setup calls demonstrating no-actor-context invocation is possible, not as evidence of an existing production caller.
grep -rn "Definitions.activate(" lib/ (excluding lib/letflow/design/) still shows exactly the one router call site after the fix -- the design's text must not contradict this.

§3.2's table rows for Letflow.Identity.create_user/2, update_user_profile/3, update_user_status/3, create_group/2, create_token/3, revoke_token/2 all state an explicit actor_id: nil disposition (not 'not verified this session' or any other deferral phrasing), each pointing to one stated decision/justification subsection rather than six repeated explanations.

The new Identity actor_id disposition does not contradict AC2 (AC2 names only definition activation, instance cancellation, and task completion -- no Identity operation) -- state this explicitly, do not just assume it.
The Task-create row's actor_id note is left unchanged (still tied to OQ-1's already-accepted open call-site location, not re-litigated).

All sections not named in points 2-3 above (§1, §1.2, §1.3, §2, §4, §5, §6, §7, §8, §0 traceability matrix, OQ-1, OQ-2, OQ-3, and §3.1a's point 1 / Decision (b) point 1 reasoning about AC11) are byte-identical to the version already passed -- verify via diff, do not re-derive.
Zero literal Elixir/SQL implementation code in the design doc -- confirmed no new code fences introduced.

CRITICAL: this handoff's top-level status field is exactly one of PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED, and context is a top-level OBJECT, not a nested wrapper -- grep/confirm before committing, documented recurring bug across this project.
